name: Phenibut

lead: Phenibut is a derivative of the neurotransmitter GABA developed in the Soviet Union in the 1960s. It is a prescription drug in Russia and some neighbouring countries for anxiety and insomnia, and is sold online elsewhere as a supplement or 'nootropic'. In looksmaxxing forums it is used to lower social inhibition and boost confidence before going out, so you come across as more sociable.

It acts mainly as an agonist at GABA-B receptors, as baclofen does but with lower affinity, and the R-enantiomer also binds the alpha-2-delta subunit of calcium channels, as gabapentin does. A phenyl ring lets it cross the blood-brain barrier, unlike plain GABA. Published human evidence is limited, largely Soviet-era work, animal studies and case reports.

paras: Users take it occasionally before social events to feel looser and more talkative. Effects are felt within hours, and communities discuss spacing out use because tolerance builds.

Reported effects include sedation, nausea, dizziness and next-day hangover. Tolerance builds quickly, and case reports describe withdrawal with rebound anxiety, insomnia, hallucinations, seizures and psychosis. It potentiates alcohol, opioids and other depressants. In the US the FDA determined in 2023 that it is not a lawful dietary ingredient, and several countries have banned or scheduled it.

angle.text: Forum users take phenibut as a 'low inhib' drug for social ease, expecting more confidence and better reactions from others. Its tranquilizer effects are documented, as are tolerance and withdrawal; published human trial data are scarce.

lead: Phenibut (beta-phenyl-gamma-aminobutyric acid) is a central nervous system depressant structurally related to the neurotransmitter GABA. It was developed in the Soviet Union and entered clinical use in Russia in the 1960s as a tranquilizer with cognition-enhancing ('nootropic') properties [1][2][3].

It remains a prescription medicine in Russia and some neighbouring countries for anxiety, insomnia and other conditions, while elsewhere it is sold online as a supplement and is used non-medically for anxiety reduction and euphoria [1][3][4]. In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed chiefly as a 'low inhibition' aid for social situations [5][6].
Published human evidence is limited: reviews rely heavily on Soviet-era studies, animal work and case reports, and describe tolerance, dependence and withdrawal in heavy users [2][4][7].
infobox: Rx in Russia and some CIS states; banned or controlled in several countries; unapproved drug in the US [1]

paras: In Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Georgia and Latvia, phenibut is approved for anxiety, insomnia and a range of other indications including asthenia, alcohol withdrawal, post-traumatic stress and motion sickness, per Wikipedia's summary of prescribing information [1]. A 2001 review described it as a tranquilizer and nootropic introduced into clinical practice in Russia in the 1960s [2]. It was included in Soviet spacecraft medical kits from 1975 [1].

Outside licensed countries it is sold online as a supplement, often for self-medication of social anxiety, and users seek anxiolysis, sociability and euphoria [1][4]. A 2016 survey-based review documented online availability, patterns of use, desired effects and acute toxicity [4]. Its appearance relevance is indirect: forum users describe it as a way to appear more confident or approachable.

Phenibut is primarily a GABA-B receptor agonist with some GABA-A activity [2]. Its affinity at GABA-B is far lower than baclofen's, and the R-enantiomer is the active form [3][8]. R-phenibut also binds the alpha-2-delta subunit of voltage-dependent calcium channels and showed gabapentin-like antinociceptive effects in animal tests [9]. Soviet-era studies reported dopaminergic effects, but the mechanism is described as unclear [1][2].

Wikipedia reports oral bioavailability of at least 63% at a 250 mg dose and an elimination half-life of about 5.3 hours, with most excreted unchanged in urine, and notes that published human pharmacokinetic data are sparse [1].

Reported effects include sedation, nausea, irritability, dizziness, headache and, at high doses, incoordination and next-day hangover [1]. Overdose case descriptions include severe drowsiness, vomiting, low blood pressure and fatty liver changes, with no specific antidote; treatment is supportive [1][4]. Phenibut can potentiate alcohol, opioids and other sedatives [1].

Tolerance develops readily with repeated use. A 2019 literature review and case report described acute withdrawal featuring rebound anxiety, insomnia, agitation, hallucinations and seizures, and baclofen has been used in managing phenibut dependence [1][7]. Contraindications listed for the licensed drug include pregnancy, breastfeeding, liver failure and young age [1].

Controlled modern human trials for anxiety or social confidence are largely absent from the literature. A 2001 review summarised mostly Russian-language clinical and preclinical work and noted anxiolytic and nootropic effects with comparisons to other tranquilizers [2]. Pharmacology studies in animals compared the isomers [8] and examined calcium-channel binding [9]. A 2016 study characterised use, desired effects and toxicity in non-medical users rather than testing efficacy [4]. A 2019 review collected withdrawal case reports [7].

In the US phenibut is an unapproved drug; the FDA determined in 2023 that it is not a dietary ingredient, making supplements containing it misbranded [1]. Australia placed it in Schedule 9 in 2018, and Hungary, Italy and France have added it to controlled lists, while Canada and the UN have not scheduled it [1]. Supplement products in the US have been found to contain anywhere from none to over 1,100 mg per serving [1].

On looksmax.org, users describe phenibut as a way to feel less inhibited and more confident when socialising [5][6]. Posters report both enthusiastic anecdotes and gastrointestinal side effects, and note that tolerance builds quickly [5]. Others in the same threads attribute the perceived social benefit to placebo or to alcohol-like disinhibition [6]. Community members also discuss obtaining it across borders and combining it with other substances, which the research literature identifies as a risk factor [1][4].
